label: Bible Study
prompt: Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in _____!
verse: Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!
note: A Song of Degrees for pilgrims headed to Jerusalem — brotherly harmony, compared to precious oil and mountain dew.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: But Jesus beheld them, and said unto them, With men this is impossible; but with God all things are _____.
verse: But Jesus beheld them, and said unto them, With men this is impossible; but with God all things are possible.
note: Said right after the camel-through-the-needle line. Impossible for men, possible with God — big difference.

label: Sunday School
prompt: And when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks, and laid them on the fire, there came a _____ out of the heat, and fastened on his hand.
verse: And when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks, and laid them on the fire, there came a viper out of the heat, and fastened on his hand.
note: Shipwrecked on Malta, Paul gathers firewood and a viper latches on — he shakes it into the fire, unharmed.

label: Deep Water
prompt: Now when Daniel knew that the writing was signed, he went into his house; and his _____ being open in his chamber toward Jerusalem, he kneeled upon his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did aforetime.
verse: Now when Daniel knew that the writing was signed, he went into his house; and his windows being open in his chamber toward Jerusalem, he kneeled upon his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did aforetime.
note: Daniel knew the lions' decree was signed and still prayed toward Jerusalem, windows open — not a protest, just his habit 'as aforetime.'

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship one with another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son _____ us from all sin.
verse: But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship one with another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanseth us from all sin.
note: 'Cleanseth' is present tense in the Greek — it keeps on cleansing, not a one-time rinse.
